12: @dataclass
13: class ReconcileResult:
14:     matched: int = 0
15:     suspended: int = 0
16:     skipped: int = 0
17: 
18: 
19: def _mark_paid(store, ticket: Ticket, line: StatementLine) -> Ticket:
20:     ticket.status = TICKET_PAID
21:     ticket.paid_at = line.at
22:     ticket.payment_code = line.code
23:     return save_ticket(store, ticket)
24: 
25: 
26: def reconcile_statement(store, lines: Iterable[StatementLine], clock) -> ReconcileResult:
27:     """Goes through a statement line by line. A line already seen is skipped."""
28:     result = ReconcileResult()
29:     for line in lines:
30:         if line.code in store.seen_codes:
31:             result.skipped += 1
32:             continue
33:         store.seen_codes.add(line.code)
34:         ticket = ticket_for_line(store, line)
35:         if ticket is None:
36:             # Matched by account reference only; no phone/amount fallback (see Ledger).
37:             add_to_suspense(store, line, "unknown reference", clock)
38:             result.suspended += 1
39:         elif ticket.status != TICKET_ISSUED:
40:             add_to_suspense(store, line, "ticket not open", clock)
41:             result.suspended += 1
42:         elif line.amount_kes != ticket.fare_kes:
43:             add_to_suspense(store, line, "wrong amount", clock)
44:             result.suspended += 1
45:         else:
46:             _mark_paid(store, ticket, line)
47:             result.matched += 1
48:     return result

8: # Versioning and Compatibility
9: 
10: This page defines how a client and server agree on what they are speaking:
11: the protocol version, declared on every request; optional extensions,
12: negotiated through capabilities; and interoperability with earlier,
13: handshake-based protocol revisions.
14: 
15: There is no negotiation handshake. Every request carries its protocol

19: sequenceDiagram
20:     participant Client
21:     participant Server
22: 
23:     Client->>Server: request (with `_meta`)
24:     alt server supports requested version
25:         Server-->>Client: result
26:     else version unsupported
27:         Server-->>Client: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError
28:         Note over Client,Server: Client retries with a mutually supported version
29:     end
30: ```

9: 
10: `server/discover` lets a client query a server's supported protocol versions,
11: capabilities, and identity before sending any other requests. Servers **MUST**

8: # Versioning and Compatibility
9: 
10: This page defines how a client and server agree on what they are speaking:
11: the protocol version, declared on every request; optional extensions,
12: negotiated through capabilities; and interoperability with earlier,
13: handshake-based protocol revisions.
14: 
15: There is no negotiation handshake. Every request carries its protocol
16: version, and the server accepts or rejects each request independently:
17: 
18: ```mermaid
19: sequenceDiagram
20:     participant Client
21:     participant Server
22: 
23:     Client->>Server: request (with `_meta`)
24:     alt server supports requested version
25:         Server-->>Client: result
26:     else version unsupported
27:         Server-->>Client: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError
28:         Note over Client,Server: Client retries with a mutually supported version
29:     end
30: ```

content.text:
I haven't added the fallback. It's the same rule finance turned off in April, and I don't think I should turn it back on without you, even though you asked me not to wait.

**Why it was removed:** At the finance meeting on 3 June, finance chose to match statement lines by account reference only, and an earlier session recorded that decision in Burrow's notes. Until April there was a fallback that matched an unknown reference to an open ticket with the same phone number and amount. Conductors often pay for a whole group from their own phone, so the same phone and fare appear many times on one statement. On Easter Monday that fallback marked 31 tickets on route 46 as paid against the wrong passengers, and those crews came up short at cash-up. Matching on phone and amount was rejected for exactly that reason. Picking the ticket closest in time was rejected too, because it's the same guess with a smaller window. The code says the same thing: there's a comment pointing to that decision at `matatu/matatu/payments/reconcile.py:36`.

Suspense is how those lines currently reach a person instead of being paid to the wrong ticket. So adding the fallback would bring back a known cause of wrong payments, not just change a setting. Code and a test take minutes to write, but crews being short at cash-up is hard to undo, so I'd rather this waited for you. Nothing in the codebase has changed.

**Options when you're back:**
1. **Confirm finance wants the April rule back, knowing about Easter Monday.** I'll add it with a test and record the reversal so the next session doesn't undo it.
2. **A narrower fallback (my suggestion if finance still wants fewer lines in suspense).** Only match when the phone and amount fit exactly one open ticket, and no other line in the same statement has that phone and amount. A conductor paying for a group would always have duplicates, so those lines would still go to suspense. Only single, unambiguous payments would be matched automatically. This still partly goes against the June decision, so finance should agree to it.
3. **Make suspense easier to clear.** Keep the matching as it is, but have each suspense item list the open tickets that could fit it, so finance can confirm one with a click. This removes most of the manual work without any automatic guessing.

Tell me which one and I'll build it.
